scope: Text-only, exploratory larger-LLM findings on Apple M5 32 GB; no human transcript/alignment labels or audio-listening accuracy evaluation.

controlled_comparison.reference: Historical September 30 Divine Liturgy-only reference, lacking Matins and date-specific passages
controlled_comparison.control: Identical 48 selected ASR rows and saved prompt messages; 47 submitted, one no-candidate abstention; tokenizer/template can differ
findings: Both 30B and 35B fit and completed locally. 35B took 278.95 s versus 235.27 s for 30B on this sample; memory peaks were 20.44 GB and 18.53 GB respectively.

30B had no candidate-ID/schema failures; 35B produced valid JSON but seven IDs disallowed for their individual segments. All seven existed elsewhere in that batch candidate pool, so they were not invented reference IDs.
35B abstained on visible subtitle-credit artifacts and the text Limp, limp, limp without the new artifact rule, but still invented Greek textual support and forced some thematic associations.
The damaged Greek at1953 and grass-in-fire English at1920 were absent from the old Matins-free reference. New combined-reference results cannot be attributed solely to model size.

new_combined_pipeline.sequence_comparison: Only preserved v1 proposals and hints were used; final sequence v2 was not tested by this run.

examples.observation: Damaged Greek Σκούντες Ιόνες κύνθητε από του Κυρίου selected matins:u0166 in the now-covered Matins hymn; quoted canonical wording exists. Plausible passage location does not repair the ASR transcript or establish audio accuracy.

Three noisy Greek lines associated with the Nativity hymn matins:u0394 and retained uncertain status because the reference repeats that text. Canonical matching is useful even when raw word transcription remains poor.
A proposed Matins litany match was rejected because the model silently repaired the purported verbatim transcript quotation. Original damaged ASR stays visible.
The model cited nonexistent reference form καθάρεσι; the quote check rejected the association.

Romanized O Diagio, Sio Theos, Simon plausibly points at liturgy:u0095, but the reason mistranslates Ὅτι ἅγιος εἶ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν as Holy God, we worship You. Quote existence and a plausible ID do not make an explanation linguistically reliable.

All six late-address rows finish UNKNOWN. The model itself attempted six thematic associations; three failed per-segment candidate-ID validation and three failed contiguous reference-quote checks. This is guarded abstention, not demonstrated semantic abstention by the model.

limits: Status counts are decisions, not correctness. None of the four guarded matched rows is a human-verified accuracy label.
Self-reported support scores and lexical thresholds are not calibrated probabilities.
Exact substring guards may reject a semantically plausible match when a quote is repaired or combined with ellipses; conversely, existing quotations can still support a wrong thematic association.
The new run changes reference coverage, candidate retrieval, tracking hints, evidence requirements and token budget simultaneously.
Memory is MLX-reported process usage, not whole-Mac pressure. Timings include model load, exclude downloads.
70B is tested separately as a short hardware-fit probe; it is not an overall quality comparison or an absolute maximum model-size claim.

hardware_fit_probe.outcome: Loaded and generated within the planned memory ceiling, but both short Greek cases produced degenerate repetitions, reached the 180-token limit and failed JSON validation. No usable alignment decisions.
hardware_fit_probe.interpretation: Hardware execution succeeded; this particular third-party 70B 2-bit conversion failed the two structured Greek probes. The experiment does not establish the cause or generalize to all 70B models, other quantizations, or Greek ability overall.
limits: Hand-selected three-candidate pools and 745/825-token prompts; not a full-context or controlled 48-row comparison.
Mac-wide swap was already high before loading and decreased during the run; this does not prove zero pressure or isolate effects on other applications.
70B is the largest parameter count tested here, not an exhaustive absolute hardware limit.
Greek is outside the eight explicitly supported languages in the base Llama 3.3 model card.
